In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipid-renin hypothesis is not valid.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipid-renin interaction is not the major factor that determines the PRR in normal human plasma.
the variation of PRR in human plasma is not due to circulating lipid-renin interactions, but rather is due to the variation of endogenous substrate.
the presence of lipid-renin inhibitors in normal human plasma has not been demonstrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PRR is dependent on the concentration of substrate, and the addition of substrate can increase PRR in normal plasma.
the lipid-renin inhibitor theory should be re-evaluated and that the use of acetonesoluble renin inhibition in normal human plasma should be abandoned.
the lipid-renin inhibitor concept should not be accepted until it has been confirmed by other investigators using different techniques.
